title: Graceful reservation decay and transient-noise dampening for dedicated clusters
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Follow-up ticket created after the Feb 11 capacity incident where a dedicated cluster experienced cascading reservation shrink and tenant evictions. This work adds a controlled decay mechanism, a short-lived grace window to ignore transient usage dips, and a smoothing layer for burst credits to reduce oscillation between reservation autosizer and the tenant governor.
incident_summary: On 2025-02-11 at ~03:10 UTC a combination of a noisy tenant spike and aggressive reservation-decay logic caused repeated reservation reclaims on a subset of dedicated GPU pools. That led to elevated tail latency for impacted tenants and several soft evictions that required manual remediation. The incident lasted ~47 minutes; remediation included pausing the autosizer and rolling back a recent reserve-decay config change.
root_cause: Three factors combined: 1) Reservation decay used a short half-life and immediately reduced allocations after rapid short-lived drops in utilization. 2) Burst tokenbucket thresholds were low and had no hysteresis, allowing rapid consume/restore cycles that amplified the autosizer signal. 3) Telemetry lacked a compact reservation-churn metric, so the control loop responded to noisy signals without aggregate damping.
action_items: Implement a grace-period (configurable) before reservation decay reduces committed capacity
Add hysteresis to burst tokenbucket refill so short spikes don’t produce oscillatory allocation changes
Introduce an EWMA-based smoothing layer to feed the autosizer rather than raw minute-by-minute utilization
Create a reservation-churn metric and alert when churn exceeds threshold for 5m/30m windows
Deploy synthetic tenant load to canary clusters to validate smoothing and hysteresis under controlled noise
Update dedicated runbooks with fast rollback steps for autosizer/config changes and checklist for eviction recovery
Instrument lease/reclaim traces to root-cause future incidents faster (span IDs in telemetry)
Ship UI indicators in Console showing reservation-decay config and current churn score for each pool
implementation_plan: Phase A (code): add 'decay_grace_seconds' and 'decay_hysteresis_pct' to autosizer config; default grace = 300s
Phase A tests: unit tests for decay timer and hysteresis logic; integration test harness with synthetic spikes
Phase B (burst): tune tokenbucket refill to include a 2-step refill hysteresis and minimum steady-state reserve
Phase C (telemetry): emit 'reservation_churn_v1' and expose in Prometheus/Grafana; build alert rule
Phase D (console): small Console patch to surface new config and churn metric (read-only initially)
Phase E (docs/runbook): publish a 1-page postmortem summary and update dedicated-cluster runbook with rollback cookbook
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated; enable on staging clusters first
Canary: enable on 5% of dedicated pools with synthetic tenant traffic for 72 hours
Observe churn metric, eviction rate, tail latency; if below thresholds, expand to 25% for another 48 hours
Full rollout to all dedicated pools after 7 days of stable telemetry and signoff from SRE
Provide a rollback playbook: flip feature flag, revert autosizer config, and notify customers via status page if any disruption occurs
testing_plan: Unit test coverage >= 90% for decay and hysteresis code paths
Integration test simulating alternating 30s-90s noisy bursts to ensure no eviction after smoothing
Load test with synthetic tenants at 2x expected peak for 1 hour to validate latency SLOs
Chaos experiment: inject a noisy tenant in canary to verify that new logic contains oscillation without global impact
monitoring: Alert: churn > 0.25 for 5m and evictions > 1/min -> P0 alert to SRE
Dashboard: dedicated-pools/stability showing churn, evictions, tail latency, autosizer-decisions
On-call playbook step added: check churn, freeze autosizer, evaluate recent commits/PRs
runbook_changes: Add 'freeze_autosizer' runbook command and escalation flow to SRE leads
Document eviction recovery procedure including 'soft-restore' to previous reservation and immediate customer notifications
Add post-incident checklist to attach telemetry snapshots and recent config rollouts for future RCA
risks: Too-conservative grace window may increase cost by holding excess reservation during legitimate sustained drops
Incorrect hysteresis parameters could mask real degradation for a short time, delaying autosizer corrective action
Feature-flag misconfiguration during rollout could leave some pools unprotected while others are protected, complicating root cause analysis
